basis: 14 conversations from chat, 1–30 July (no Claude Code or Cowork)

example.text: For instance, you come back to the same conversation over several days and build on it, rather than starting fresh.

areas.label: What you hand over
areas.summary: You hand over the routine work and keep what needs judgement.
areas.info: Choosing what AI takes on, and what you hold on to yourself.

quotes.text: I'll do the structure myself, but you can write a first draft of the sections

areas.anchor: Hands routine work to AI, keeps what needs judgement.

areas.label: How you ask
areas.summary: You set format and constraints up front, and correct quickly when the answer misses.
areas.info: How clearly you explain goal, format and examples, so the answer lands first time.

quotes.text: Write it as a table with three columns, and keep each line under 15 words
That's too long — same content, half the length, and drop the intro

areas.anchor: Sets goal, format and constraints up front most of the time.

areas.label: How you judge the answer
areas.summary: You catch clumsy wording fast. Errors in the content itself go through.
areas.info: Reading the answer critically and catching errors, especially when it looks convincing.
areas.anchor: Reacts to what reads wrong; corrects wording, tone or structure rather than substance.

areas.label: Care and data
areas.summary: You avoid the obvious, and there is no habit behind it yet.
areas.info: Confirming an answer before you rely on it, and looking after what you put in.
areas.self_report: I don't put client names in, but I haven't thought much beyond that.

moves.text: When an answer looks right, check one thing in it you can verify. A number, a name, a date.
Once a week, ask what argues against the answer. You will see fast where it was thin.

why: Your checking happens after something already looks wrong. You correct wording quickly and well. Nothing in these conversations shows you checking a figure or a claim before you use it, and in two cases a wrong number went through. That is the one step missing.
